**Finding: deviation (WARRANTY) — redline validated and submitted.**

What I found:

- **§ 9 "TrueLink Warranties" (p0059–p0060)** is TrueLink's only express warranty, and it is limited to Y2K date processing. There is no conformance-to-documentation warranty, no malicious-code warranty, no compliance-with-laws warranty, and no warranty remedy.
- **§ 11 "Standard of Care" (p0069)** requires only "the same degree of care, skill and prudence customarily exercised by it for its own operations" — a self-referential standard rather than an industry standard, and it attaches no repair/replace/refund or re-performance remedy.
- **The disclaimer (p0076)** is prefaced "EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY SET FORTH IN THIS AGREEMENT," so it does **not** swallow express warranties — no carve-out needed. This is not a walk-away "AS IS" clause; the gap is simply that there is no express performance warranty to preserve.

Because the agreement lacks both a conformance period and any remedy, it fails even the fallback (90 days software / 30 days services with remedies), so a redline was warranted rather than a rationale note.

Redline (inserted after p0060, preferred position): TrueLink warrants (a) professional and workmanlike performance of Hosting, Support and other services consistent with industry standards; (b) 12-month conformance of the Interface and related software to documentation and specifications; (c) freedom from malicious code; and (d) compliance with applicable laws — with Client's remedy being re-performance, repair/replacement, or refund of fees paid, at TrueLink's option. The comment offers a 90-day conformance period as the fallback if TrueLink pushes back.
